sections.overview: Trogloraptor marchingtoni is a cave-associated spider and the described member of its family, Trogloraptoridae.
sections.identification: It is yellow-brown, with a small body and flexible hooked tips on its legs.
sections.habitat: It is known chiefly from deep caves in Oregon, including Oregon Caves National Monument and Preserve.
sections.diet: Its natural prey remains unknown; captive spiders did not feed on the moths, crickets or spiders offered in one account.
sections.behavior: A few strands of silk hang from cave ceilings, and researchers hypothesize that the spider may hang there and snatch airborne prey.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted do not provide a species-specific account of its mating or egg-laying.
sections.ecology: Its hooked leg tips may help seize prey, but their exact role and the spider’s feeding ecology remain uncertain.
sections.conservation: The cited park account documents a narrow known cave range but gives no formal conservation category.

sources.title: An extraordinary new family of spiders from caves in the Pacific Northwest
